name: Nethanel
overview: Nethanel was a male Levite known as the son of Jedaiah, belonging to the priestly line descended from Aaron. His role as a priest highlights his participation in the religious duties and heritage of the tribe of Levi. This connection situates him within the sacred service of Israel according to the biblical record in Nehemiah 12:21.
namesAndTitles: The name Nethanel means "G-d has given," reflecting a theologically significant meaning that emphasizes divine provision. This proper name is recorded in Nehemiah 12:21 and was not given directly by God but carries a clear expression of faith in God's generosity.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Nethanel as the son of Jedaiah, establishing a direct paternal relationship noted in Nehemiah 12:21. Beyond this, no additional family relationships are recorded for him.
scriptureSignificance: Nethanel's importance lies in his identification as a priest descended from Aaron, underscoring his role in maintaining the Levitical priesthood during the period documented in Nehemiah. His mention contributes to the genealogical and priestly records that affirm the continuity of God’s covenantal worship among Israel. This serves as a reminder of the faithfulness of God’s provision through the generations of His chosen servants.
